summary: Name-search results (a Smart Folder's too) and Recents follow the files that other programs add, remove, rename or write. crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs: each index's fff-search watcher reports into a shared `Changes`: two counters (`listed`: files added, removed, renamed, and rescans; `recent`: those plus each write report, for files Recents would show) and a log of the last 512 files that came or went. New API: `Engine::follow_changes` (subscribe every index whose watcher is up; off the window's thread), `changes` (two atomic loads), `changes_for(req, numbers, lists)` (which changes are a search's business, or None for anything), `only_written_since`, and the hidden test hook `report_change_for_test`. `Engine::rescan` counts a change to everything. `RootIndex.followed` is shared by an index's copies. `recents()`'s skip rule is now `recents_skips`, shared with `recents_shows`. src/finder/mod.rs: `check_for_changes` (the two-second look, and window activation) calls `check_index_for_changes` first. `Behind` holds a list's pacing: `seen`, `stale` (`Stale::Files` or `Stale::Everything`), `catching_up`, `misses`, `wait`, `looks_behind`, `quiet_looks`. A name search asks `changes_for`, waits for a look with no more news (half a minute at most), then runs again through `start_search(debounce, stale, cx)` with no spinner and no redraw; `run_search` is now a wrapper around it. The answer replaces the results only if `Stale::shows_in` says the changed files show. Answers that come out unchanged back off 1, 3, 7 … 127 looks; a minute of looks with no news forgives that. Recents has `reload_recents` and `read_recents`. `poll_index_status` asks the indexes to report once they are finished (75 tries, 400 ms apart). tests/common/mod.rs: `Open.watch`, `Ui::look_for_changes`, `rescan`, `reindex`, `report_change`, `engine`.
changelog: Search results and Recents follow files that other programs add, remove, or rename, as open folders already did. A search by name, a Smart Folder's too, runs again by itself a few seconds after a file it lists, or could list, comes or goes. What's selected stays selected, and results the file made no difference to are left as they are. Recents is read again when a file it would show is added, removed, renamed, or written to. A search by contents still waits for Refresh (Cmd+R), and with Watch folders for changes off everything waits for Rescan.
behaviour_changes: A name search updates by itself when another program adds, removes or renames a file it lists or could list (in the searched folder, of the kind, with the words in its path inside the search location). Smart Folders, the file chooser and every tab included. No spinner, selection and scroll kept, a selected item that is gone loses its selection. In the real debug app under Xvfb with a real watcher I saw a new file listed 3.1 s after it was made, a removed one gone and another listed 3.1 s after, and one 4.3 s after; the selected row stayed selected.
Results that the changed files made no difference to are left as they are: no redraw, no reshuffle.

While files that are the search's business keep coming at every look, the search waits for them to stop, but for half a minute at most (16 looks): then it runs anyway. (Review fix; before it waited for as long as they came.)

Reruns that come out unchanged are spaced 2, 4, 8 … 128 looks apart (a little over four minutes), until the results change, a new search is typed, Refresh, or (review fix) a minute of looks passes with no file that is the search's business, after which it follows closely again and catches up at once with what it still had waiting.

A result renamed in the window is not searched for again when the index reports the rename, and neither is any file renamed where it is under a folder the search lists. (Review fix; each used to cost a rerun that came out unchanged and one more step of holding back.)

Recents updates by itself while it shows: files added, removed, renamed or written to are picked up at the first look with nothing more, and after half a minute at the latest (review fix: two files written in turn, as two downloads are, used to keep Recents as it was until one finished; in the real app the second file went first 31.7 s into fifty seconds of such writing). A single file being written goes first without waiting (first within about 3 s in the real app). While it is first, further writes read nothing and its row keeps the size and date it showed. Reports that leave Recents unchanged hold it back 1, 3, 7 … looks only until a wait passes quietly.

Rescan refreshes results and Recents in every window and tab, and reliably after a short rescan too. During a rescan or an index build a window with a name search runs it again quietly every 600 ms or less until the index is done.
With Watch folders for changes off nothing is live; Rescan updates results and Recents.

Cost, real debug app with software rendering, 100 ticks = 1 s of CPU, started with --query so no caret blinks: search open and idle 20 s = 11 to 21 ticks; 360 unrelated files made and removed in 20 s = 18; a matching file made and removed again in another folder every 5 s for 60 s = 59, which is the idle rate, with the next real match listed 6.3 s after it came. Recents: idle 20 s = 14; two files written in turn for 20 s = 15; the first file written to 100 times in 20 s = 16. Per look and window, nothing changed costs two atomic loads.

docs/manual.md: the "Open folders refresh on their own" paragraph (now also: every half minute or so while files keep coming, and closely again after a minute without them), the Searching paragraph, Recents, the Smart Folder sentence, and the search.watch row.
fffinder-core API: new Engine::follow_changes, changes, only_written_since, changes_for, report_change_for_test. Engine::rescan also counts a change.
left_out: Contents searches wait for Refresh, as planned.
A new near miss with a typo is not noticed until Refresh: it has no words in its path to go by. The manual says so.

Temporary indexes (a folder outside every search location) report only if a search runs after their watcher is up. Small folders are covered by the retry 600 ms later; larger ones are not live until the next keystroke or Refresh. No extra polling was added for them.
A rescan put off behind a running scan can leave results stale in the windows other than the one where Rescan was chosen, until the next event. The verifier's known risk.

Rows of files changed in place keep their old size and date until the list is next replaced, as folders already do. That includes a file that stays first in Recents (a download shows the size it had when it first appeared).

Filters typed into the search (`*.pdf`, `!draft`, `git:modified`, folder tokens) are not weighed when a new file is judged: every new file in the folder and of the kind is the business of a search with no words, so such a search backs off quickly on a busy disk. The Kind menu's kinds are weighed.

A file removed, or moved away, under a folder the search lists still runs the search again (the folder may have gone with it), and that usually comes out unchanged. Only renames in place are known not to matter.

When anything may have changed (a rescan, fff-search's own rescans, more than 512 changes between two looks, more than 256 files waiting), the answer is compared in order, so a list cut among many equal matches is replaced by another cut of them. That is the run-to-run difference sorted-search-results found, showing after such events.

No test for the rule that results from an index still being built are always replaced by the next quiet answer (`partial` in start_search's answer): such an index can't be staged without timing. It is reasoned only: without it a quiet answer could leave `search_stats.indexing` true for good.
`cargo clippy --features term` was not run: nothing in src/term uses what changed (grep), and no signature it calls changed.
macOS and Windows were not compiled here. No cfg-gated code and no existing signature changed.

review_fixes: src/finder/mod.rs, `Behind::forgive_after_quiet`: a search held back by reruns that came out unchanged was held back until its results changed, a new search or Refresh. Misses from single files hours apart added up, so a search left open ended up as much as four minutes behind for as long as it showed. Now thirty looks in a row with no file that is the search's business (a minute) set the misses and the wait back to nothing, and what was waiting runs at once. Under files that keep coming it backs off as before, so the steady cost is at most one rerun a minute, and one in about four minutes on a busy disk.

src/finder/mod.rs, `Behind::due` and `looks_behind`: a list waited for a look with no news for as long as news kept coming. Recents never showed two files written to in turn until one was done (seen in the real app, with a single download showing at once), and a search open during a long copy showed nothing new until it ended. Now a list is behind for 15 looks at most before it is made again anyway. Unchanged answers still back off, so files that keep coming and change nothing cost one run in about four minutes.

crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs, `changes_for`: a file that came and that the search lists already is no longer its business. The window puts a renamed result under its new name at once, so the index's report of it a moment later ran the search again for nothing and counted as a miss; so did the report of a file that a search had already picked up while it ran.

crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs, `changes_for`: a renamed file has not left the folders that both its paths are in, so those are not looked up as folders that may have gone. Any rename inside a folder the search lists used to run the search again.
tests: five new window tests and three new engine assertions (list under tests). Each fix was removed again on its own, seven mutations in all, and each was noticed by the tests named for it.
docs/manual.md and the commit message say the new pacing; one comment in check_index_for_changes corrected (the set of shown paths is also looked up for files that came).

Rebase onto four new trunk commits: two conflicts in docs/manual.md (Recents, where show-in-enclosing-folder-key added a sentence, and the Smart Folder paragraphs, which smart-folder-save-and-leaks rewrote), resolved to keep both sides' text.
notes:
Checked. check.sh printed CHECK OK on the trunk commit 153eb8f: 657 passed in 16 test binaries, 3 of 3 known root-only failures (638 on the trunk before it, plus the 19 tests above). The implementer's commit was 5070970 on 323f173; the trunk moved by four commits while I reviewed (c28f42d, 66d4fad, a6b81fc, 60df179). `git push . HEAD:search-ui-polish` fast-forwarded 60df179..153eb8f and `git push origin search-ui-polish` went through; `git ls-remote origin` reads 153eb8f.

How it was checked. I read the changed functions whole (engine: RootIndex::follow, Changes, follow_changes, changes_for, only_written_since, rescan, recents; window: Behind, Stale, check_index_for_changes, reload_recents, start_search and its answer and retry, poll_index_status, location_changed) and fff-search's watcher (events are per file, sent after the index is updated, ignored files never; a rename seen in one batch is one Renamed event; a full rescan sends Rescan and swallows the batch; fff rescans by itself once 1024 new files have come since the last scan). Every caller that starts a search goes through run_search or run_new_search, which reset `Behind`; `search_gen` moves only in set_query("") and start_search, so a quiet run that is dropped can't leave `catching_up` set past the next search. With src/finder/mod.rs put back to the trunk's, 8 of the implementer's 9 window tests failed (the ninth is the contents guard); with the whole non-test change reversed the tests do not build (no `changes`, no `report_change_for_test`). The two real-watcher tests passed 10 and 15 runs in a row at a load average near 10. I ran the real debug binary under Xvfb on a copy of the demo folder with a real watcher and read its rows through the control server (FFFINDER_SERVER_TCP=1: the scratch path is too long for a Unix socket), with keys through XTest: see behaviour_changes for what I timed.

The three ways I thought it most likely to hurt, and what I found. (1) Background work on a busy home folder: bounded. Nothing changed costs two atomic loads a look; changes that are none of a search's business cost a lock and a scan of at most 512 entries on the window's thread; reruns are held to the paces above. (2) The list changing under the hands: only where a changed file shows; selection goes by path and scroll is not touched. After a rescan or a flood of changes a list cut among equal matches can come back as another cut (left_out). (3) Trusting a list that has silently stopped following: this is where the review fixes are (never forgiven, never run while files kept coming). What is left is in left_out.

For the briefs still to come:
- adhoc-index-feedback: `RootIndex` has a new field `followed: Arc<Mutex<bool>>` (set it where you build one; the test scope_follows_the_base_spelling builds one by hand). `follow_changes` subscribes `indexes.adhoc` too, and a discarded index's subscription goes with its picker. A temporary index reports only if `follow_changes` is called after its watcher is up, and today the only caller for it is the search's own call right after `engine.search`. If you add a wait or a status for temporary indexes, call `engine.follow_changes()` (off the window's thread) when one finishes, and large folders outside the search locations become live too.
- recents-walk-index: `recents()` skips by `recents_skips(part)`, and `recents_shows(base, path)` uses the same rule to decide which reported files count for Recents. Keep the two the same: a file Recents lists that `recents_shows` denies is never read again for. The window reads Recents only in `read_recents` (src/finder/mod.rs), for the first read and the quiet ones, and `reload_recents` shows a list only when its paths or their order differ. A written file is taken to go first: `check_index_for_changes` skips the read while the one file written to is `listing.first()`.
- typo-fallback-near-miss (lane-g, at work): `changes_for` judges a new file by `strict_words(req)`: every fuzzy word of the search, its letters in order, in the file's path inside the index folder. That is right as long as a search outside the typo fallback lists nothing else. The engine test what_a_search_lists_is_among_the_changes_that_matter_to_it checks it for thirteen searches and ends with the exception, a near miss for `atlsa`, which it expects the search to list and `changes_for` to pass over. If your change stops listing that near miss, change that last block; if it lets anything without the words into a list that has matches with them, `changes_for` has to follow.
- result-tie-break (lane-b, at work): `Stale::Everything.shows_in` compares the answer's paths in order after a rescan. A fixed order among ties means fewer lists replaced for nothing; nothing here needs changing.
- files-changed-off-thread: with watching on, a result removed by another program drops out by itself a few seconds later, but `files_changed`'s own `results.retain` is still what makes the window's own operations show at once. If the check moves off the window's thread, apply its answer by path and only for the same `search_gen`: a quiet rerun can replace `results` meanwhile.
- stale-rows-on-place-change: `location_changed` sets `recents_behind = Behind::as_of(..)` and drops `recents_task`; keep both before the read. `check_index_for_changes` leaves Recents alone while `self.loading`, and reads it quietly through `reload_recents`, which never sets `loading`.
- filter-stale-keep-set: a quiet rerun whose answer is shown goes through `rebuild_rows` and so through `apply_filter_to` like any rerun; one that isn't shown touches nothing.
- search-start-no-flash, empty-state-messages (lane-c, at work): the search's body is `start_search(debounce, stale, cx)`; `run_search` calls it with None. A quiet run (`stale` is Some) leaves `searching` false and doesn't notify, and `search_stats` is replaced only by an answer that is shown, so messages and placeholders see nothing of it. First-run rules belong in the path where `quiet` is false.
- stale-previews-and-cancel: a quiet rerun compares which paths are listed, not their sizes or dates, so a file changed in place keeps its old row, and a preview cache stamped from the row won't see a new stamp from it.
- restore-session-tabs: every tab's browser looks every two seconds whether it shows or not, and a tab with a name search runs it again in the background for the files that are its business.
- search-settings-without-effect, regex-content-search: `follow_changes` reads `search_settings().watch`; contents searches are not followed and `check_index_for_changes` returns for them first.

Found, not fixed:
- Once the search field has had the keyboard, the window is drawn about twice a second for good, with nothing happening: 31 calls of render_content in 16 s under gdb with no search, no reload and no row rebuilt, after Ctrl+F and then Escape in a window that showed a folder. Idle CPU was 6 ticks in 15 s in a fresh window and 109 after (debug build, software rendering). It looks like the field's caret going on blinking after the keyboard has left. It is on the trunk without this change (no query, no Recents: check_index_for_changes does nothing there).
- While a search shows, the folder it was made in is still looked at, and each change in it reads the folder again and rebuilds the rows twice (load_listing, then load_folder_stats), which draws the window: 12 reloads and 24 rebuilds for 12 files made and removed there. The results don't change by it.
- The sidebar's "N files indexed" is read only while an index is being built, so it stays at the old count as the watcher adds files.
- `Engine::rescan` rescans the search locations only, not the temporary indexes.
- After the window renames a result to a name that no longer has the search's words, the row stays in the results until the search next runs (as before this change).
